title: Cardcaptor Sakura
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ten-year-old Sakura Kinomoto accidentally frees the magical Clow Cards from a book in her father's library, and the guardian beast Kero chooses her to recapture them. With her best friend Tomoyo filming her and designing costumes, and rival-turned-ally Syaoran Li, she seals each card and later transforms them into her own Sakura Cards. Around the magic, the series centers on many kinds of love, presented without judgment.
life_message: Love in all its forms, and the trust that 'it will definitely be all right', carry you through anything.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Rivalry with Syaoran turns to friendship; no insult is avenged.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Sakura follows rules of magic and school, while love is free of social rules.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Close family (father, Toya) balanced with friends and classmates.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Guardians and wizard heirs, but relationships are egalitarian and gentle.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Inherited magic and Clow's legacy in a modern town.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Love, costumes and feelings take center stage; no material worries.

folkways.japan: Respect for family, school rituals and Tomoyo's devoted service reflect Japanese norms; its open treatment of many loves reflects CLAMP's own stance.

delivery.evidence: Many forms of love shown without judgment through the cast's romances; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: Acceptance of love in many forms is carried by the characters, with no worldview condemned.

winners_losers: Sakura and every sincere lover in the cast win; no worldview is condemned. Sympathy goes to love in all its forms.
